Programme Educational Objectives (PEOs) of B.Tech. in COMPUTER
SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
PEO1 Professional Excellence and Higher Learning: Graduates will establish successful careers in
industry, government, academia, and research organizations, and pursue higher studies and lifelong
learning in emerging areas of computing.
PEO2 Research, Innovation and Leadership: Graduates will engage in research, innovation, en-
trepreneurship, and leadership activities to develop impactful computing solutions and contribute
to technological advancement.
PEO3 Ethics and Societal Contribution: Graduates will uphold professional ethics and demonstrate
social responsibility by contributing to sustainable development, societal well-being, and national
progress.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/BCS/Cur./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate15.10 (a) /July 2026 - 5/103

Programme Outcomes (POs) and Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
of B.Tech. in COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
PO1 Engineering Knowledge: Apply knowledge of mathematics, natural science, computing, engineering
fundamentals and an engineering specialization as specified in WK1 to WK4 respectively to develop
to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2 Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature and analyze complex engineering
problems reaching substantiated conclusions with consideration for sustainable development. (WK1
to WK4)
PO3 Design/Development of Solutions: Design creative solutions for complex engineering problems and
design/develop systems/components/processes to meet identified needs with consideration for the
publichealthandsafety,whole-lifecost,netzerocarbon,culture,societyandenvironmentasrequired.
(WK5)
PO4 ConductInvestigationsofComplexProblems: Conductinvestigationsofcomplexengineeringproblems
using research-based knowledge including design of experiments, modelling, analysis & interpretation
of data to provide valid conclusions. (WK8)
PO5 Engineering Tool Usage: Create, select and apply appropriate techniques, resources and modern engi-
neering & IT tools, including prediction and modelling recognizing their limitations to solve complex
engineering problems. (WK2 and WK6)
PO6 The Engineer and The World: Analyze and evaluate societal and environmental aspects while solving
complexengineeringproblemsforitsimpactonsustainabilitywithreferencetoeconomy,health,safety,
legal framework, culture and environment. (WK1, WK5, and WK7)
PO7 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics, human values, diversity and inclu-
sion; adhere to national & international laws. (WK9)
PO8 Individual and Collaborative Team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or
leader in diverse/multi-disciplinary teams.
PO9 Communication: Communicateeffectivelyandinclusivelywithintheengineeringcommunityandsoci-
ety at large, such as being able to comprehend and write effective reports and design documentation,
make effective presentations considering cultural, language, and learning differences
PO10 Project Management and Finance: Apply knowledge and understanding of engineering management
principles and economic decision-making and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader
in a team, and to manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO11 Life-Long Learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability for i) independent
andlife-longlearningii)adaptabilitytonewandemergingtechnologiesandiii)criticalthinkinginthe
broadest context of technological change. (WK8)
PSO1 AdvancedComputingSystems: Applycomputerscienceprinciplestoanalyze,design,anddevelop
efficient computing solutions for complex real-world problems.
PSO2 Data-DrivenandScalableTechnologies: Developintelligent,data-driven,andscalablecomputing
solutions using modern technologies and computing paradigms.
PSO3 Research, Innovation, and Technology Development: Apply research methodologies and inno-
vative thinking to develop impactful technologies and solutions for societal, industrial, and national
needs.

6. Activity Credits (AC)
A minimum of 40 Activity Points must be earned to obtain the 10 credits required in the curriculum; these credits are
not counted towards CGPA. The scheme of activity points, as approved by the Senate, is announced at the start of
the first semester. A minimum of 20 points must be earned by the end of the 4th semester and 40 points by the end
of the 7th semester.

Programme Outcomes (POs) and Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs)
of B.Tech. in COMPUTER SCIENCE AND ENGINEERING
with Specialization in AI and Data Science
PO1 Engineering knowledge: Apply the knowledge of mathematics, science, engineering fundamentals,
and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2 Problem analysis: Identify, formulate, research literature, and analyze complex engineering prob-
lems reaching substantiated conclusions using first principles of mathematics, natural sciences, and
engineering sciences.
PO3 Design/development of solutions: Design solutions for complex engineering problems and design
system components or processes that meet the specified needs with appropriate consideration for the
public health and safety, and the cultural, societal, and environmental considerations.
PO4 Conduct investigations of complex problems: Useresearch-basedknowledgeandresearchmeth-
odsincludingdesignofexperiments, analysisandinterpretationofdata, andsynthesisoftheinforma-
tion to provide valid conclusions.
PO5 Modern tool usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern en-
gineering and IT tools including prediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an
understanding of the limitations.
PO6 Theengineerandsociety: Applyreasoninginformedbythecontextualknowledgetoassesssocietal,
health, safety, legal and cultural issues and the consequent responsibilities relevant to the professional
engineering practice.
PO7 Environment and sustainability: Understand the impact of the professional engineering solutions
in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable
development.
PO8 Ethics: Apply ethical principles and commit to professional ethics and responsibilities and norms of
the engineering practice.
PO9 Individual and team work: Function effectively as an individual, and as a member or leader in
diverse teams, and in multidisciplinary settings.
PO10 Communication: Communicate effectively on complex engineering activities with the engineering
community and with society at large, such as, being able to comprehend and write effective reports
and design documentation, make effective presentations, and give and receive clear instructions.
PO11 Project management and finance: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the engineering
and management principles and apply these to one’s own work, as a member and leader in a team, to
manage projects and in multidisciplinary environments.
PO12 Life-long learning: Recognize the need for, and have the preparation and ability to engage in
independent and life-long learning in the broadest context of technological change.
PSO1 Acquire strong fundamentals of computer science, artificial intelligence, and data science expressed
through effective problem-solving techniques, algorithmic thinking, and intelligent system design.
PSO2 Exposure to modern computational platforms, emerging AI technologies, and interdisciplinary appli-
cations to fulfill and enhance the industry, research, innovation, and entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Programme Outcomes (POs) and Programme Specific Outcomes (PSOs) of
B.Tech. in ELECTRONICS AND COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING
After completion of B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering, the Graduates will be able to
PO1 Engineering Knowledge: Applytheknowledgeofmathematics, science, engineeringfundamentals,
and an engineering specialization to the solution of complex engineering problems.
PO2 Problem Analysis: Identify, formulate, review research literature, and analyse complex engineering
problemsreachingsubstantiatedconclusionsusingfirstprinciplesofmathematics,naturalsciencesand
engineering sciences.
PO3 Conduct Investigations of Complex Problems: Use research-based knowledge and research
methods including design of experiments, analysis and interpretation of data, and synthesis of the
information to provide valid conclusions for complex problems
PO4 Modern Tool Usage: Create, select, and apply appropriate techniques, resources, and modern
engineering and IT toolsincludingprediction and modelling to complex engineering activities with an
understanding of the limitations.
PO5 Environment and Sustainability: Understandtheimpactoftheprofessionalengineeringsolutions
in societal and environmental contexts, and demonstrate the knowledge of, and need for sustainable
development.
PSO1 Possess sound theoretical and practical knowledge of Electronics and Communication Engineering.
PSO2 Apply the knowledge and skills to design and develop state-of-the-art hardware and software systems
as well as products.

5. Projects (P)
The major project represents the culmination of study towards the B.Tech. degree. It is offered in two parts –
Project-1 and Project-2 – and gives students the opportunity to apply and extend the knowledge gained across the
programme. The work may be analytical, simulation-based, hardware design, or a combination, in an emerging area
of ELECTRONICS AND COMMUNICATION ENGINEERING, carried out under the supervision of a department

faculty member. Project work may be carried out individually or in groups (size decided by the department) and may

6. Activity Credits (AC)
A minimum of 40 Activity Points must be earned to obtain the 10 credits required in the curriculum; these credits are
not counted towards CGPA. The scheme of activity points, as approved by the Senate, is announced at the start of
the first semester. A minimum of 20 points must be earned by the end of the 4th semester and 40 points by the end
of the 7th semester.

5. Projects (P)
The major project represents the culmination of study towards the B.Tech. degree. It is offered in two parts –
Project-1 and Project-2 – and gives students the opportunity to apply and extend the knowledge gained across the
programme. The work may be analytical, simulation-based, hardware design, or a combination, in an emerging area
ofMATHEMATICSANDCOMPUTING,carriedoutunderthesupervisionofadepartmentfacultymember. Project
work may be carried out individually or in groups (size decided by the department) and may build on an industrial
problem identified during an internship.
6. Activity Credits (AC)
A minimum of 40 Activity Points must be earned to obtain the 10 credits required in the curriculum; these credits are
not counted towards CGPA. The scheme of activity points, as approved by the Senate, is announced at the start of
the first semester. A minimum of 20 points must be earned by the end of the 4th semester and 40 points by the end
of the 7th semester.

with Specialization in Cyber Security
PEO1 TechnicalLeadershipandResilientSystemsArchitecting: Graduateswillestablishthemselves
as successful cybersecurity professionals and technical leaders capable of conceptualizing and design-
ing resilient systems and secure software architectures. Leveraging advanced investigative analysis
and modern cybersecurity tools, they will apply adversarial tactics and cyber warfare principles to
proactively harden complex ecosystems.
PEO2 Ethical Governance, Continuous Innovation, and Professional Excellence: Graduates will
demonstrate professional excellence and accountability by integrating ethical principles, cyber laws,
andgovernance, risk,andcompliance(GRC)frameworksintotechnicalandorganizationalleadership.
They will engage in applied research and continuous learning to dynamically adapt to rapidly shifting
security paradigms, seamlessly navigating next-generation challenges.
PEO3 Human-Centric Security and Public Welfare: Graduates will champion digital safety and so-
cietal well-being by developing inclusive, human-centric security architectures. They will leverage
advanced investigative methodologies to mitigate digital threats against communities, ensuring the
protection of vulnerable populations and fostering enduring public trust in technological ecosystems.

PO4 Professional Ethics, Governance, and Communication: Apply ethical principles, legal man-

the complete penetration testing lifecycle, conducting sophisticated digital and smartphone forensics,
and managing Security Operations Centre (SOC) workflows leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) to

uate advanced security mechanisms for complex, emerging ecosystems spanning cyber-physical infras-
tructures, decentralized networks, and intelligent AI-driven platforms by applying adversarial tactics,
threat emulation, and cyber warfare principles to proactively harden architectures.

Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam (IIIT Kottayam or Institute) is estab-

class human resources in IT and which can harness the multidimensional facets of IT in various
domains. To develop new knowledge in information technology and to provide manpower of
globalstandardsfortheinformationtechnologyindustry. IIITKottayamiscommittedtoemerg-
ing amongst the foremost institutions in information technology and allied fields in the global

oping competent and capable youth imbued with the spirit of innovation and entrepreneurship
with a social and environmental orientation. The Institute pursues these objectives through ap-

ORDINANCE
Eligibility for admission, admission policy and procedure shall be decided from time to time by the
Senate/BoardofGovernors(BoG)oftheIndianInstituteofInformationTechnologyKottayam(hence-
forth referred to as Institute), following the guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education (MoE),
Government of India (GoI).
• Instituteoffersregularfull-timeB.Tech./B.Tech.(Hon.) DegreeProgrammeswithnormalduration
of 4 years (8 semesters) and Dual Degree B.Tech.+M.S. Programmes with normal duration of 5
years (10 semesters).
• TheawardoftheB.Tech./B.Tech.(Hon.) degree/DualdegreeB.Tech.+M.S.shallbeinaccordance
with the regulations of the Senate of the Institute.
• The Senate/BoG of the Institute has the right to modify any regulations stated from time to time.
REGULATIONS
R.1.0 Admission
R.1.1 The number of seats in each branch of the programme for which admission is to be made in
the Institute will be decided by the Senate of the Institute. Seats are reserved for candidates
belonging to the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes, Economically
Weaker Section and Physically Challenged candidates as per the orders of MoE, GoI, from
time to time. A few seats may be offered to Foreign Nationals, Indians living abroad and
other categories in accordance with the rules and procedures issued by the MoE, GoI and the
Institute from time to time.
R.1.2 Admission to the B.Tech. programmes in any year will be based on the performance in Joint
Entrance Examination (JEE) Main, subject to change as per the orders from MoE, GoI.
R.1.3 The eligibility criteria shall be consistent with the ordinance.
R.1.4 The central seat allocation authority (as decided by orders of MoE, GoI, from time to time)
will provide a merit list for the general category of students and a separate merit list for
candidates belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Economically Weaker Section,
Physically Challenged and Other Backward Classes.
R.1.5 Candidates have to fulfil the medical standards required for admission as set out in the
Information Brochure by the Institute or by any other body or organization entrusted by
MoE/the Institute.
R.1.6 The selected candidate will be admitted to the B.Tech. programme after the student fulfils
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 3/35

all the admission requirements set by the Institute available on the Institute web site or as
indicated in the letter of admission and after payment of the prescribed fees.
R.1.7 If,atanytimeafteradmission,itisfoundthatacandidatehasnotfulfilledalltherequirements
stipulated in the offer of admission, or it is found that a candidate has furnished any false
information, the Institute may revoke the admission of the candidate and report the matter
to the Senate.
R.1.8 In all matters related to admission to the B.Tech. programme, the decision by the Institute
or by any other body/organization entrusted by MoE/the Institute and its interpretation
given by the Chairman of the Senate shall be final and binding.
R.2.0 B.Tech./B.Tech.(Hon) Degree/B.Tech.-M.S. Dual Degree Programme
R.2.1 Every programme specialisation will have a curriculum with syllabi consisting of theory, prac-
tical, project work, etc., as approved by the Senate and with categories as given below:
• Institute core courses comprising basic courses on Mathematics, Engineering Sciences,
Professional Communication, Soft Skill & Personality Development, Entrepreneurship,
Management, Economics, and Finance, etc.
• Theprogrammecorecourses(ofthespecialisation)consistingofboththeoryandpractical
courses on the engineering/technology in the relevant areas.
• The programme elective courses (of the specialisation) consisting of courses on the en-
gineering/technology in the relevant areas, where the students will have the option to
choose the courses as per their interest.
• Open elective courses consisting of courses for holistic and skill development like Design
Thinking & Innovation, etc.
• Projects relevant to the concerned specialisation approved by the Department.
• Activity Credits (AC) comprise courses like Environmental Studies, Liberal Arts and Co-
curricular/Extra-curricular activities like Sports, Institute approved club activities, etc.,
fromwhichthestudentsareexpectedtoobtainaminimumof40pointstowards10credits
which are not counted for CGPA. The details of activities counted towards AC and the
corresponding points will be issued by the Institute from time to time.
R.2.2 The complete programme will consist of courses as per the approved curriculum distributed
overeight(forB.Tech. &B.Tech.(Hons))/ten(forB.Tech.-MS)semesterswithtwosemesters
per year.
R.2.3 Foundation courses will generally be covered in the first two years (four semesters). From
the fifth semester onwards students focus more on respective stream core courses and other
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 4/35

electives. In the case of the B.Tech.-MS programme, the fifth year will be devoted to thesis
by research.
R.2.4 At the end of the fourth semester, the students having a minimum of 8.0 CGPA should
make their choice regarding the programme they would like to opt for, such as B.Tech. or
B.Tech.(Hon) or B.Tech.-MS.
R.2.5 Credits are assigned to the courses based on the following general pattern: one credit for each
lecture period; one credit for each tutorial period; one credit for each laboratory or practical
or project session of two periods/sessions.
R.2.6 The curriculum of any specialisation of the B.Tech. programme is designed to have a total
of 160 credits. The minimum credits for the award of the B.Tech. degree are 160 with a
minimum CGPA of 5.5. For B.Tech.(Hon.) and B.Tech.-MS dual degrees, the minimum
credits for the award are 180 and 200 respectively with a minimum CGPA of 8.0.
R.2.7 The syllabi and curricula of the programmes are subject to revision from time to time, based
on the suggestions from the curriculum committee with the approval of the Senate.
R.2.8 No semester shall have more than seven lecture-based courses and four laboratory courses/
projects as prescribed in the curriculum, carrying more than 30 credits.
R.2.9 The medium of instruction, examination and project reports will be English.
R.3.0 Registration and Enrolment
R.3.1 Each academic year has two semesters, namely, Odd Semester (August–November) and Even
Semester(January–April). Exceptforthefirstsemester,registrationofasemesterwillbedone
during a specified week before the commencement of the semester (pre-course registration).
R.3.2 From the second semester onwards all students have to enrol within a specified duration at
the beginning of a semester as per the academic calendar. A student will be eligible for
enrolment only if the student satisfies R.8 and will be permitted to enrol only if the student
has cleared all dues to the Institute, Hostel, Library and other sections up to the end of the
previous semester, provided he/she is not debarred for enrolment by a disciplinary action of
the Institute.
Late registration/enrolment will be permitted with a fine as decided from time to time up
to a specified time from the last date specified for registration in the academic calendar.
R.3.3 Theregistrationportalcontainsthecoursecode,coursename,numberofcreditsandcategory
foreachcoursetakeninthatsemester. Thestudentmakesthechoiceofcourseinconsultation
with his/her Faculty Advisor.
R.3.4 The maximum credits that can be registered by a B.Tech. student in any semester is the
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 5/35

normal credits of the concerned semester as per the relevant curriculum. A few exceptions
are:
(i.a) Students who are repeating failed courses/crediting dropped courses (R.4.0)/courses
withdrawn (R.7.0), along with regular courses, shall be permitted to register for a max-
imum of two courses (failed/dropped/withdrawn) in addition to the normal credits of
the semester except in the VII and VIII semesters.
(i.b) Students can register for courses up to a maximum of 30 credits including the normal
courses of the semester and failed/dropped (R.4.0)/withdrawn (R.7.0) courses in the
VII and VIII semesters.
Before making the registration, students shall check the timetable to avoid any slot overlap
of the courses registered. Registrations shall be done with the prior approval of FA/HoD.
(ii) Auditing extra courses: Students are also eligible to take extra courses (only for audit
purpose and not for CGPA) apart from the normal courses prescribed in the curriculum,
viz., one course each in the 5th, 6th and 7th semesters and not more than two courses in
the 8th semester subject to a maximum of 30 credits (total for the semester), provided
the student has no backlog and has earned a CGPA of ≥ 7.0 at the end of the previous
semester. Before making the registration, students shall check the timetable to avoid any
slot overlap of the courses registered. Students taking extra courses should obtain the
prior approval of the Dean through FA/HoD. These courses will be shown in the grade
card only if passed (with a grade U). These will not be considered for CGPA calculation.
R.3.5 No withdrawal from any of the courses registered will be allowed except as per regulation
(R.4.0 or R.7.0).
R.4.0 Slow Pace Learning
The curriculum for any semester, except for the final semester, will normally carry credits between 15
and 30.
If a student finds their academic load heavy in any semester, or for any other valid reason, the student
may drop one or two courses (after proper discussion with FA) within the stipulated date as per the
academic calendar, with the written approval of his/her Faculty Adviser/HoD. However, the students
should ensure that the total number of credits registered in any semester should enable them to earn
theminimumnumberofcreditsasspecifiedinR.17.0tocompletetheprogrammewithinthemaximum
duration of the programme permitted as per R.9.0.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 6/35

R.5.0 Faculty Advisor (FA) and Class Committee (CC)
R.5.1 To help the students in planning their courses of study and for getting general advice on
the academic programme, the Institute will assign a certain number of students to a Faculty
member who will be designated as their Faculty Advisor.
R.5.2 Every class of the B.Tech. programme will have a Class Committee consisting of Faculty and
students’ representatives.
R.5.3 The constitution of the Class Committee will be as follows:
• One Faculty (who is not taking any course for the class) nominated by the Dean (Aca-
demics) to act as the Chairperson of the Class Committee.
• Faculty members of each of the lecture/lab based courses.
• Class Representatives (minimum two, out of which one shall preferably be a girl) of the
respective class.
• Faculty Advisors of the respective class/batch.
R.5.4 The basic responsibilities of the Class Committees are:
• Finalisation of the course plan, attendance and evaluation policies of all courses as per
the academic rules. These should be announced to the students at the beginning of the
semester and presented in the first class committee by the faculty.
• To review periodically the progress of the classes.
• To discuss problems concerning the students and make suitable recommendations to im-
prove the academic performance of the students.
• Identification of students with poor performance and low attendance and reporting the
matter to FAs and HoDs for appropriate actions.
• The class committee meeting without student members, at the end of the semester, would
finalize the grades of the students for each course.
• The Committee shall meet at least thrice during the semester. The Dean (Academic) or
nominee or HoD shall have the right to be present in any Class Committee meeting. The
Chairperson of the committee or his/her nominee shall record the proceedings of each
meeting and the Chairperson shall communicate a copy of the minutes of each meeting to
the HoD/Dean (Academic) for any further action.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 7/35

R.6.0 Attendance, Condonation and Course Feedback
R.6.1 Students are expected to attend all the classes. Students should have a minimum of 80%
attendance in a course to become eligible for writing the end-semester examination of the
course. Students shall check their attendance details with the faculty after the mid-semester
examination. A list of students who are likely to have attendance shortage will be announced
in the class committee meeting after the mid-semester examination for the information of the
FA/class representatives.
The faculty handling a course must finalise the attendance 3 calendar days before the last
instructional day of the course in the semester. The particulars of all students who have
attendance less than 80% in that course will be announced in the class by the corresponding
faculty.
The percentage of attendance shall be calculated based on the number of classes conducted
from the date of commencement of the semester as per the academic calendar (except for first
semester students). In the case of first semester students, it shall be counted from the date
of admission of the student to the Institute or start of the classes, whichever is later.
Those students with attendance less than 80%, for any course registered in a semester, will
be eligible to get their shortage of attendance condoned and hence to appear for the end-
semester examination for that course only if the student applies for condonation subject to
the following conditions:
• the attendance in that semester for the course concerned, without applying any condona-
tion, is not less than 65% of the total classes handled for that course;
• the attendance after considering all the leaves approved (as per R.6.2) is 80% or above, of
the total classes handled for that course.
Provisionalpermissionmaybegiventoappearfortheend-semesterexaminationifthestudent
has submitted all the relevant documents for the appropriate leave and paid the condonation
fee.
R.6.2 If a student could not attend any of the classes due to medical issues or any other compelling
reasons, or for essentially participating/volunteering in any events/functions/extra-/co-
curricular activities approved by the Institute, a leave application needs to be submitted to
the FA/HoD.
(i) All applications for any leave shall be submitted to FA within five instructional days after
returning from leave, or on or before the last instructional day of the semester, whichever
is earlier, failing which it will not be considered.
(ii) Application for leave on medical grounds must be submitted to FA with necessary treat-

with endorsement from the Institute medical officer for the period of leave applied for.
It is also expected that the student shall inform the course faculty before proceeding on

FA and approved by the concerned HoD.
(iii) Applicationfordutyleaves(maximumlimittobespecified)forparticipating/volunteering

(R.6.2), shall be sent to the HoD/Academic section.
R.6.4 Those students whose attendance in a course is 80% or above, after considering the approved
leaves(R.6.3), maybepermittedtowritetheend-semesterexaminationthroughcondonation.
Application for the condonation shall be submitted to FA with the payment slip (for the
condonationfee—anominalpenaltyamountasdecidedbytheInstitute)forrecommendation
before the commencement of end-semester examinations, for the approval of HoD/Dean. If
the student fails to submit the application with the payment slip for condonation, he/she
will not be permitted to write the end-semester examination and will be awarded an L grade
for that course.
R.6.5 Students having an attendance percentage still less than 80 after considering all the approved
leaves(R.6.3)willbeawardedanLgradeforthecourse. ThestudentswhohaveanLgradein
atleastonecoursewillhavetorepeatthecoursesinwhichhe/shehasinsufficientattendance,
whenever it is offered next.
R.6.6 For every course, attendance in the end-semester examination is mandatory. In cases where
the student does not attend the end-semester examination without any prior appropriate
approval under exceptional circumstances (see R.11.1), he/she will be considered to have
failed in the course and it will be counted as a backlog.
R.6.7 All the students are expected to complete the course feedback form. Online course feedback
by students will be taken with full confidentiality for every course. Submission of the course
feedback is essential for the issue of the hall tickets for the end-semester examination.
R.7.0 Withdrawal of a Registered Course
Withdrawal of a registered course(s) in a semester is usually permitted/enforced under very special
cases,forexample,duetoprolongedillness. AWgradeisgivenforthecourse(s)inthesecircumstances
and the student is asked to repeat the concerned course(s) with the same course code, taking all the
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 9/35

examinations when it is offered next. The new grade obtained by the student will be taken into
consideration and appear in the transcript. However, the previous W grade will also appear in the
transcripttillthecourseissuccessfullycompleted. AWgradewillnothaveanyeffectinthecalculation
of SGPA and CGPA. If a student has a W grade in a registered course in a particular semester, SGPA
will be calculated based on the grades obtained in other registered courses of that semester. A similar
rule will apply to CGPA as well.
R.8.0 Essential Requirement to Continue the Programme
A student should not have more than 2 backlogs at the end of each year and should not have any
disciplinary actions and no dues, to continue their studies during the programme. If a student has
more than 2 backlogs, as stated above, a choice may be provided to the student to either repeat the
failedcoursesinthesummerterm(R.15.0)orregisterforthefailed/additional(inthecaseofelectives)
courses in the upcoming semesters (R.3.4), or to exit/get terminated from the programme. If his/her
average credits earned is less than 12 in a year (for students under slow pace learning, R.4.0) but not
more than 2 backlogs, he/she has to register for the courses not yet registered as per the curriculum,
in the subsequent semester.
R.9.0 Maximum Duration of the Programme
A student is ordinarily expected to complete the B.Tech. or B.Tech.(Hon) programme in eight
semesters, and the dual degree programme (B.Tech.-MS) in ten semesters. However, a student may
complete the B.Tech. programme at a slower pace by taking more time (with the approval of the Insti-
tute), but in any case not more than 12 semesters excluding semesters on temporary discontinuation
as per R.10.0.
R.10.0 Temporary Discontinuation from the Programme
(i) A student may be permitted by the Director to discontinue temporarily from the programme
for a maximum of two semesters for reasons of ill health or other valid reasons, based on the
recommendation from FA and HoD. For this break of study due to illness, all necessary medical
reports and medical certificates from the doctor treating the student, giving definite reasons for
the break of study and its duration, shall be produced. The medical certificate should be duly
endorsed by the Institute Medical Officer. Before joining back, a fitness certificate from the
doctor who treated the student, with endorsement from the Institute Medical Officer, has to be
submitted.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 10/35

(ii) The students desirous of initiating a start-up venture shall submit their business proposal to
the Academic section through the FA/HoD concerned. The proposal shall be scrutinized by
an Institute Level Committee for Innovation, Entrepreneurship and Start-ups constituted by the
Director. Based on the recommendation of the committee, the Director may approve the proposal
for start-up formation. Once the start-up is registered through IIITK (only) and has initiated
activities,thestudentsconcernedcansubmitanapplicationforanacademicbreakofonesemester
or a maximum of two semesters for their start-up activities, if they desire. The Dean (Academic)
will take appropriate action for temporary discontinuation based on the recommendation by the
HoD. The academic break shall be given initially for one semester and a further extension of one
more semester will be given based on a review of the progress and recommendation by the HoD.
(iii) Incaseofachangeinthecurriculum/syllabi,astudenthastoregisterfortheapprovedequivalent
courses (meeting the credits) as per the revised curriculum/syllabi as per the advice of the FA,
whenever the student is allowed to continue the programme after the period of discontinuation.
(iv) Temporary discontinuation shall be sanctioned only for one semester at a time. A student shall
not be permitted to avail two semesters of discontinuation continuously in a single sanction;
where a second semester of break is required, a fresh application shall be submitted with the
recommendation of the FA/HoD, and the extension may be granted subject to the approval of
the competent authority, within the overall limit of two semesters specified in (i) above.
(v) Students proceeding for temporary discontinuation are required to maintain the Institute regis-
tration by paying the fees applicable for keeping the registration alive till they resume normal
academic activities. Once they join back after temporary discontinuation, fees applicable for
regular students shall be paid at the time of registration.
(vi) If a student wants to leave the programme, he/she will be issued with the grade cards of all the
completed courses and credits earned will be uploaded in ABC. No credit transfer certificate will
be issued from the institute.
R.11.0 Make-up Examination
R.11.1 Make-up examination for the end-semester: The incomplete grade ‘I’ is a transitional grade
which will be given to students who are unable to appear for the end-semester examinations
with prior approval under exceptional circumstances (e.g., hospitalisation under serious med-
ical reasons with an appropriate medical certificate from a Medical Officer endorsed by the
Institute Medical Officer) as recommended by the course instructor/faculty advisor/Head
of the Department and approved by the Dean (Academics). A make-up examination will be
given to the students provided they meet the attendance requirements as per R.6.0 and other
academic requirements as per the rules and regulations of the Institute. All applications for
make-up examinations shall be submitted to FA, and when approved by the HoD, the FA
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 11/35

shall inform the academic section for giving necessary instructions to the course faculty con-
cerned for conducting the make-up examinations. The list of students permitted to appear
for the make-up examinations for the end-semester examinations shall be published by the
department/academic section.
Theactualgradeafterthemake-upexaminationwillbetakenandwillreflectinthegradecard,
replacing the ‘I’ grade. In case the student obtains an F grade in the make-up examination,
the student shall repeat the end-semester exam.
R.11.2 Make-up examination for the mid-semester: The make-up is permitted for the mid-semester
examination only for very essential valid reasons like (i) approved medical leave for hospitali-
sation with a certificate from a Medical Officer endorsed by the Institute Medical Officer, or
(ii) any prior approved leave by the Chairman, Senate, for participating in approved national
events, or (iii) any prior approved leave by the FA/HoD due to emergency critical situa-
tions with proof of inability to attend the examination certified by a gazetted officer. The
make-up examination for the mid-semester shall be conducted based on the mutual conve-
nience between the students and course faculty during the semester before the end-semester
examination.
R.11.3 There will not be any make-up examination for the components other than mid- and end-
semester examinations, in the curriculum.
R.12.0 Assessment and Grading
A. Assessment
R.12.1 Continuous assessment will be adopted for the assessment of all the courses. In this regard,
tests,quizzes,assignments,tutorials,courseprojects,etc.,appropriatetothecourse,andmid-
and end-semester examinations will be conducted. The Senate will decide from time to time
on the system of assessment for each course in each semester. The number of assignments,
tutorials, presentations, quizzes, course projects, reports, etc., with the weightage, shall be
decided by the course faculty and as announced in the first class committee.
A general guideline for the assessment procedure of a theory course with respective weightage
is given below.
• Continuous Assessment (Assignment, Quiz, Tutorials, Course Project, etc.): 25–45%
• Mid-Semester Examination — minimum 90 minutes duration: 15–25%
• End-Semester Examination — minimum 180 minutes duration: 40–50%
However, if any change in the above guideline is required, the details of the weightage of
marks for these within-semester term evaluations have to be announced to the students, in
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 12/35

consultation with the Class Committee at the beginning of the semester. The total weightage
for Continuous Assessment within the semester and mid-semester examinations together will
be between 50% and 60% and should not be more than 60%. The weightage for the end-
semester examination will be the remaining.
R.12.2 For practical courses, 70% weightage will be given for experiments through continuous eval-
uation and 30% weightage will be given for written/viva examinations at the end of the
semester. The split-up components and weightage of continuous evaluation will be decided
by the faculty instructor and as announced in the first class committee.
R.12.3 TheassessmentofactivitiesbythestudentsaspartofActivityCredits(AC)shallbefinalised
by the faculty in-charge of the event/instructor as per the guidelines issued by the Senate
from time to time.
R.12.4 Project Evaluation: The B.Tech. project work is carried out in two stages (BTP-I and
BTP-II), each spread over a semester — 7th and 8th semesters.
(i) At the end of the first stage (BTP-I), the student is required to submit a preliminary
brief report of their work by a prescribed date to the Project Coordinator and present
it to a Project Evaluation Committee (PEC) constituted by the concerned department,
including the guide, as a seminar. Both the report and presentation shall be as prescribed
by the department. Out of the total credits assigned to the project, 30% of the weightage
comes from the Project guide and the remaining 70% is awarded by the other members
of the Project Evaluation Committee (PEC).
(ii) The first stage (BTP-I) work can be continued in the following semester as BTP-II and
a final report has to be submitted at the end of that semester. The distribution of the

(iii) Projects done in reputed research/academic institutions/industries under an approved

(iv) The project report, prepared according to the prescribed format available in the academic

R.12.6 A student is considered to have completed a course successfully and earned the credits if
he/she secures a letter grade other than F or W or I or U in that course.
R.12.7 Grade ‘I’ will be awarded by a course faculty to a student in a course as an interim grade
when the assessment of the student in that course stands incomplete due to certain valid
reasons. Once an ‘I’ grade is awarded to a student, the concerned course faculty shall ensure
that it will be converted to a final grade before the next academic session, and the same shall
be informed to the academic section through the Chairperson, CC, and HoD.
R.12.8 Grade W will be awarded by a course faculty to a student in a course when the course is
withdrawn by the student as per R.7.0. The W grade, once awarded, stays in the record of
the student and is deleted when he/she completes the course successfully later. The grade
acquired by him/her will be indicated in the grade card of the appropriate semester.
R.12.9 Students whose attendance is less than 80% for a course in a semester will be awarded the
letter grade L for that particular course in that semester, irrespective of the marks obtained
by them for that course, unless their shortage of attendance is condoned as per R.6.0. The L
grade, once awarded, stays in the record of the student and is deleted when he/she repeats
the course and receives a pass grade later.
R.12.10 An F grade will be awarded in a course if the student failed as his/her performance is not
satisfactory for a pass grade. An F grade obtained by the student will be deleted in the grade
card once that course is successfully completed.

R.14.0 Re-count/Re-evaluation of Answer Books
For a re-count of answer books, in case any student feels aggrieved, only for theory courses, he/she
can contact the course faculty concerned within one week from the announcement of the results. The
student shall have access to his/her answer books/paper(s) of the end-semester examination, which
may be shown (only) to him/her inside the faculty cabin by the faculty concerned. In case of any
counting mistakes, and if the faculty feels that the case is genuine, he/she may re-examine the case
and forward a revised grade, if any, to the Dean (Academic) through the Chairperson of the Class
Committee/HoD with justification for the revision. The course faculty shall ensure that the decision
on the request is communicated in writing to the student within a week, if there is no change in the
published results.
Ifthestudentisstillnotsatisfied, anappealcanbesubmittedtotheDean(Academic)throughFAand
HoD for re-evaluation of the answer scripts, along with the receipt for the payment of the prescribed
re-evaluation fee, within ten working days on receipt of the communication from the course faculty.
The Dean (Academic) may arrange for the re-evaluation of the answer scripts/book by another faculty
member from a panel of a minimum of 2 examiners (faculty who have already offered the same or a
similar course) proposed by the HoD. Once the result of re-evaluation of answer scripts is intimated
by the faculty who conducted the re-evaluation to the Dean (Academic), the results obtained on re-
evaluation will replace the earlier results, only if the difference is more than 5% of the maximum
marks. Requests received for re-evaluation after the stipulated time shall not be entertained. The
result after this re-evaluation shall be final and no further process shall be permitted. There shall not
be any re-evaluation of answer scripts/books of mid-semester/repeat examinations and examinations
conducted for labs. Also, there is no re-evaluation for the projects.

R.15.0 Summer Term and Contact Courses
1) A summer term course (STC) may be offered for courses where more students received an F grade
in a course, during the summer vacation, if there are at least 5 students to take up the course.
No student should register for more than two courses during a summer term.
2) Summer term courses will be announced normally after the publication of the results of the end-
semester examinations of the even semester. A student will have to register within the time
stipulated in the announcement by paying the prescribed fees.
3) The number of contact hours in any summer term course (STC) will be the same as in the regular
semester course. The attendance requirements and the assessment procedure in a summer term
course will also be similar to the procedure for a regular semester course. The students who
received an F grade in a summer term course shall repeat the same in the subsequent semesters,
when the same is offered.
4) A Contact course may be offered during the summer vacation, ONLY to a final year student
who has obtained an F grade in a maximum of 2 courses and has completed successfully all the
remaining courses and requirements. A contact course refers to an accelerated course where the
entire classes and examinations related to a course shall be completed in 30 to 45 days’ time.
The course will be offered ONLY on the recommendation of the department, with the mutual
agreement of the faculty instructor and the student, when the student has paid the prescribed
fees and has no other pending dues to the Institute. Such final year students who wish to take
contactcoursesshouldapplytotheDean(Academic)asperthenotificationissuedbytheacademic
section, through FA/HoD.
5) No student should register for more than two contact courses during the semester or summer
period.
6) A contact course cannot be offered if a regular OR a summer course is offered on the same course
during that period.
7) The assessment procedure for a contact course will be similar to the procedure for the regular
semester course. The students who received an F grade in a contact course shall repeat the same
in the subsequent semesters, when the same is offered.
8) Withdrawal from a summer term or contact course, or refund of the fees paid, is not permitted
after the registration.
9) The maximum grade awarded in a summer term course is limited to a B grade, and that in a
contact course is limited to a C grade.

R.16.0 Repeating the Courses to Improve the CGPA to Meet the Minimum De-
gree Requirement
At the end of the programme, when the student has successfully completed the credit requirement
(as per R.17.0) but the CGPA earned is less than 5.5 (the minimum requirement for the degree), the
student is allowed to improve only those courses whose GP is less than 6.0 by repeating the courses (on
a chargeable basis) until the student earns a CGPA of 5.5 (limited to 5.5 even if it is more than 5.5)
within the stipulated maximum period (12 semesters as per R.9.0) of the programme, subject to the
approval of the Dean/Director with recommendations from FA/HoD. If they still fail to earn a CGPA
of 5.5 within the maximum period of the programme, they will be given only a course completion
certificate and not the degree certificate.
Astudentwho,attheendofSemesterVI,hasearnedaCGPAoflessthan5.0shallalsobepermittedto
repeat courses (on a chargeable basis) in which the GP earned is less than 6.0, provided the concerned
department is floating the course in that semester and free slots are available in it. Such registration
shallbesubjecttotheapprovaloftheDean/DirectorwithrecommendationsfromFA/HoD,andshall
be governed by the same conditions as R.16.1, including the capping of CGPA at 5.5.
R.17.0 Degree Requirements
R.17.1 Eligibility for the Award of B.Tech. Degree. A student shall be declared to be eligible for
the award of the B.Tech. degree if he/she has:
• Registered and successfully completed all the core courses and projects as specified in the
curriculum corresponding to the branch of his/her study.
• Successfully acquired the minimum required credits (160) with a minimum CGPA of 5.5
as specified in the curriculum corresponding to the stream of his/her study within the
stipulated time.
• Successfully completed the minimum required points (40) for the activity credits.
• No dues and no disciplinary action are pending against the student.
R.17.2 Eligibility for Award of the B.Tech.(Hon) Degree. A student shall be declared to be eligible
for the award of the B.Tech.(Hon) degree if he/she has:
• Registered and successfully completed all the core courses and projects as specified in the
curriculum corresponding to the branch of his/her study.
• Successfully acquired the minimum required credits (180) with a minimum CGPA of 8.0
as specified in the curriculum corresponding to the stream of his/her study within the
stipulated time.

ANNEXURE R.19.A
A.1 Code of Conduct
Disciplinary policies of the Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam (IIIT Kottayam) are
put in place to ensure a secure, academically enriching environment for all members of the community
and to promote civility on campus. Students of IIIT Kottayam are expected to show personal integrity,
respect for Institute resources, and respect for others’ rights, values of scholarship and teaching. Stu-
dents are expected to adhere to the Institute rules and regulations. Any violation will be handled
according to the rules set forth by the Senate and Board of Governors of IIIT Kottayam. The admin-
istrators of the Institute will notify parents/guardians if a student violates the Code of Conduct. Any
of the following shall constitute a violation of the Code of Conduct for students and makes the student
liable to disciplinary action by the Institute.
• Lack of courtesy and disorderly conduct or disruptive acts (within or outside Institute premises).
• Any act that compromises the safety/security of individuals or Institutional facilities.
• Wilful damage or unauthorized removal of Institute property.
• Unauthorized access to institutional facilities/records.
• Tampering of data/records (reading, copying or destroying).
• Any act of fraud/misrepresentation/dishonesty.
• Misappropriation of any belongings of fellow students/staff/faculty.
• Adoption of unfair means during examinations or misconduct in research.
• Infringement of personal privacy.
• Ragging in any form.
• Caste/religion/ethnicity/gender/physical disability based discriminatory behaviour/remarks.
• Sexual harassment/assault.
• Possession of banned substances or dangerous items (illegal drugs, weapons, firearms, etc.) that
endanger the safety of the student himself/herself or others.
• Any act that affects the reputation/orderly conduct of the Institute.
A.2 The Disciplinary Procedure
• The Discipline and Welfare Committee (DWC) of the Institute is constituted under the chairman-
ship of a faculty member by the Director. Depending on the issues of allegations involved, the
Chairman of the DWC may invite additional members, for example the Coordinator of a Pro-
gramme, the student’s faculty adviser/research supervisor, or the Deputy Registrar (Academics &
Administration) in case of academic related issues, to facilitate the investigation.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 23/35

• DWC will investigate the allegations of misdemeanours or violation of the Code of Conduct with-
out bias. The DWC will subsequently submit a fact-finding report and recommend disciplinary
action(s), if any, to the Dean, Student Affairs. Complaints related to caste/religion/ethnicity/
gender-specific discrimination and sexual harassment will be investigated by an appropriate com-
mittee of the Institute and will report directly to the Director.
• While hearing the disposition of the accused student(s) and witnesses, the Chairman, DWC, may
invite two senior student observers (with one woman and/or SC-ST observer if the accused stu-
dent(s) belong to the same community), from the B.Tech.-MS (5th Yr) and PhD programmes
respectively, to be present with the DWC.
• The student observers are to be invited by the Chairman, DWC, in consultation with the Dean,
Student Affairs, from a list of nominees forwarded by the Schools. The list of nominees is valid for
a year.
• The student observers shall withdraw at the conclusion of the above and may submit their remarks
(if any) in writing to the Chairman, DWC, for consideration.
• The Chairman, DWC, shall keep records of the entire proceedings of the meetings.
• All disciplinary actions shall be notified in writing to the concerned students and their parents/
guardians by the Office of the Registrar.
• A student who feels aggrieved with the disciplinary action may appeal to the Director. The appeal
has to be filed within a period of one month from the date of intimation of the disciplinary action,
stating clearly the case and explaining his/her position and reason(s) for reconsideration of the
decision.
A.3 Disciplinary Actions
• Violation of the Code of Conduct shall invite disciplinary action, which may include penalties such
as reprimand, fine, suspension/expulsion from the hostel, debarring from examinations, withdraw-
ing/withholding of scholarship/fellowship/benefits or access to Institute facilities, withholding
of grades and/or degrees, revoking of awarded degrees, suspension for a certain period or even
permanent expulsion from the Institute.
• The Senate may withhold recommendation of a student, who is found guilty of a major offence, to
the Board of Governors for the award of a degree, even if the student has satisfactorily completed
all the academic requirements.
• Lack of knowledge of the rules and regulations is not admissible as an excuse or defence for mis-
conduct/dishonesty, and shall not be a basis for leniency.
A.4 Disciplinary Action for Malpractices in Research
• Students involved in conducting research at IIIT Kottayam are expected to maintain the highest
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 24/35

standards of integrity. Any form of unscrupulous conduct will be investigated by competent au-
thoritiesandcouldwarrantavarietyofdisciplinaryactions, inseverecasescancellationofB.Tech./
B.Tech.(Hon)/B.Tech.-MS registration or even cancellation of an awarded degree at any time.
• Research misconduct can take place in many forms, including deliberate interference with the
integrity of the work of others, plagiarism, falsification of data, and fabrication of data. In partic-
ular, students are expected to observe the practice of acknowledging the source(s) of information
reproduced in their thesis, reports, publications, or seminars.
• Plagiarism includes, without citation, the appropriation of another individual(’s) text, results, or
ideas.
• Falsification includes actions such as not accurately representing research records or results, or
manipulating reagents or equipment settings, to produce a preconceived outcome.
• Fabrication includes making up data and recording them.
A.5 Code of Conduct in the Examination Hall to be Followed by the Students
All students shall read and understand the code of conduct and strictly adhere to it. Unawareness of
these rules will not stop any punishment against malpractices.
All students are hereby informed that the Institute follows a zero-tolerance policy against examination
malpractice and any malpractice attempt from the student(s) will lead to severe punishments that
include, but are not limited to:
• Awarding an F grade for the selected subjects in the examination, with or without giving a chance
of repeat examination.
• Awarding an F grade for the selected subjects in the examination and being awarded one grade less
for all the other theory courses registered in the semester.
• Awarding an F grade for all theory subjects in the examination in that semester, with or without
giving a chance of repeat examination.
• De-registration of all the courses enrolled in the current semester.
• Debarring from examinations for a specific duration like 2 or more semesters.
• Debarring from campus placement activities.
• Termination from the Institute.
Anycombinationoftheabovepunishmentsmayalsobeapplieddependingonthegravityoftheoffense.
The following instructions are to be meticulously followed by all the students in the exam hall:
1. The students must occupy their seats in the examination hall at least 15 minutes before the
examination starts. Entry to the examination hall will not be permitted 15 minutes after the
start of the examination.
IIIT Kottayam, Kerala IIITK/Acad/Reg./Ver.VIII(ADM2026)/Senate 15.10(h)/July2026 – 25/35

2. The seating arrangements made by the Institute must be strictly followed by students as they
are not allowed to make any changes. The students should be seated in accordance with their
assigned roll numbers that are displayed in the hall.
3. As per the Institute policy, you must wear the ID Card when you are on the campus and hence
in the exam halls. If by chance a student loses the Institute ID card, they must apply for a new
one. Until they receive the new ID card, they are required to obtain a duplicate I-card from the
IT Support Team (BB217) by paying the prescribed fee. No extra time will be granted if you
misplaceyourIDcardandlosetimecollectingaduplicate(aspertheabove-mentionedprocedure)
during the examination. (Digital copies of the ID card on mobile or gadgets are not valid.)
4. Students are not permitted to bring any bag, pouch, or loose or written or blank sheets other
than those permitted by the course faculty to the examination hall. Any code books/data hand-
books/other hand-outs carried by the students shall be duly attested/endorsed by the course
faculty. Any additional scribing in such materials with pen or pencil will be treated as exam mal-
practiceandispunishable. Possessionoruseofchits(includingblankpaper), notes, books, sheets,
or any information related to their course/study, in any form including writing answers/tips/
formulae/equations/algorithms/figures/sketches/block diagrams/data, etc., on the student’s
body or clothing or other wear, walls, furniture, or keeping or leaving such material at the exam-
ination venue or other surrounding areas (like toilets, windows, veranda, etc.), are considered as
malpractice and attract punishment, even if they are not using the above during the exam. It
will be the responsibility of the concerned students to keep their things/belongings which are not
permitted inside the exam hall, including mobile phones/other electronic gadgets/laptops/tabs,
etc., safe outside the examination hall. The Institute/Invigilators will not be responsible for any
loss/damage in this regard.
5. Mobile phones/laptops/tabs/smart watches/Bluetooth devices/similar electronic gadgets or
other transmitting or receiving devices, or other means of communication, or any other electronic
device, or any AI-based tools are strictly banned in examination halls. Carrying such devices to
the exam hall or nearby areas, or leaving such devices in the exam hall or nearby areas, and/or

ORDINANCE
The minimum academic qualification for admission through Central Seat Allocation (as per MHRD, Govt. of India
orders) to IIIT Kottayam (hereafter, the Institute) is a pass in the final examination of 10+2 (Class XII) or its
equivalent.
• Admission to the particular branch of study shall be as per MHRD, Govt. of India orders.
• The duration of the B.Tech programme will normally be 8 semesters, and Dual degree programme will be 10
semesters.
• The award of the B.Tech / B.Tech Honours/ B.Tech+MS dual degrees shall be in accordance with the regula-
tions of the Academic Advisory Committee / Senate of the Institute.

R.1.1 The number of seats in each branch of the B.Tech/MS programme for which admission is to be made in the
Institute,willbedecidedbyitsAcademicAdvisoryCommittee/Senate. Seatsarereservedforcandidatesbelonging

nation(JEE)MainandHSCexaminationsasperCentralBoardofSecondaryEducation(CBSE)guidelines(subject
to change as per MHRD, Gov of India, orders).

bythecommitteefromyeartoyear,theauthoritywillofferadmission,inorderofmerit,fromtheseliststocandidates

R.2.0 B.Tech/BTech(Hon)/ B.Tech-MS dual Programme
R.2.1 The programme of instruction will consist of:
• A general core programme comprising computer science/ information technologies, engineering sciences, basic
science, humanities, engineering arts, and mathematics.
• An engineering core programme introducing the student to the foundations of engineering in their branch
• An elective programme enabling the students to take up a group of courses to their interest
• Projects approved by the Department/ faculty in-charge.
In addition, a student should satisfactorily complete the prescribed PASS/ FAIL courses in Physical and socially
relevant activities.
R.2.2 The complete programme will consist of 5 categories: Humanities, Basic Sciences, Basic
Engineering, Professional Major and Electives and distributed over eight/ ten semesters with two
semesters per year.
R.2.3 First two years (four semesters) courses will be foundation courses and designated as Institute core courses.
Fifth semester onwards students focus more on respective stream core courses and other electives. In the case of
B.Tech-MS programme, fifth year will be devoted to a thesis by research.
R.2.4 At the end of fourth semester, the students should make their choice regarding the programme they would
like to opt such as B.Tech or Btech (Hon) or B.Tech-MS.
R.2.5 Every branch of the B.Tech programme will have a curriculum and course contents (syllabi) for the courses
approved by the Academic Advisory Committee / Senate.
R.2.6 Credits are assigned to the courses based on the following general pattern: One credit for each lecture
period; One credit for each tutorial period; One (two) credit for each laboratory or practical or project session of

R.5.1 Students are expected to attend all the classes. Every teaching staff member handling a class will take at-
tendance till 3 calendar days before the last instructional day in the Semester. Students should have minimum 80%
attendance.
R.5.2 The incomplete grade I is a transitional grade which will be given to the students who miss the end semester
examinations under exceptional circumstances (eg. serious medical reasons) as determined by the course instruc-
tor/faculty advisor/Head of the department and approved by the Dean(Academics). Make up examination will be
given to the students provided they meet the attendance requirements as per R.5.3 and other academic requirement
as per the rules and regulation of the institute. Actual grade after the make-up examination will be taken and will
reflect in the transcript replacing the I grade. In case the student obtains F grade in the make-up examination, the
student will be eligible to write the repeat end semester exam.
R.5.3 Students having an attendance percentage between 65% to 80%, with valid/genuine reasons may be
permitted to continue the course by paying a nominal penalty amount as decided by the competent authority. Stu-
dents having an attendance percentage less than 65 will be awarded L grade. The students who have L grade in at
leastonecoursewillhavetorepeat the courses in which he/she has insufficient attendanceintheupcoming
year. For every course, the attendance in the end semester examination is mandatory. In cases where the student
does not attend the end semester examination, he/she will be considered to have failed in the course and will be
counted as a backlog.
R.5.4 There will not be any make-up examination for mid-semester exams and quizzes.
R.5.5 Withdrawal of a registered course in a semester is usually permitted/enforced under very special cases, for
example, due to prolonged illness. W grade is given in these circumstances and the student is asked to repeat the
concerned course with same course number taking all the examinations when it is offered next. The new grade
obtained by the student will be taken into consideration and appear in the transcript. However, the previous W
grade will also appear in the transcript till the course is successfully completed. W grade will not have any effect in
the calculation of SGPA and CGPA. If a student has W gr

ade in a registered course in a particular semester, SGPA
will be calculated based on the grades obtained in other registered courses of that semester. Similar rule will apply

day of the course in the semester. The particulars of all students who have attendance less than 80% in that course
will be announced in the class by the corresponding teacher. Copies of the same should also be sent to the Dean

R.7.0 Essential Requirement to Continue the Programme
R.7.1 A student should earn not less than an average of 15 credits in every year to continue their
studies. However, in the final semester a student may earn less than 15 credits if it is sufficient for him to fulfill the
requirements for the award of the degree. If a student fails to earn at least the average 15 credits every
year, as stated above, a choice may be provided to the student to either repeat failed courses in the upcoming
year to satisfy the regulation or terminate the program.
R.7.2 A student who has not completed the physical activities credit requirements in first four semesters will
not normally be permitted to continue the programme.
R.7.3 A student should have a minimum CGPA of 5.0 calculated for the courses successfully completed at the
end of each year. Students with CGPA below 5.0 at the end of each year, may be permitted to the next semester
if he/she has less than 2 or exactly 2 backlogs. If the student has more than 2 backlogs, a choice may be provided
to the student to either repeat failed courses of the corresponding semester in the upcoming year or terminate the
program.

A student is ordinarily expected to complete the B.Tech programme in eight semesters, and the dual degree pro-

R.13.0 Conduct and Discipline
R.13.1 Code of Conduct
Disciplinary policies of Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam (IIIT Kottayam) are put in place to
ensure a secure academically enriching environment for all members of the community and to promote civility on
campus. Students of IIIT Kottayam are expected to show personal integrity, respect for Institute resources, and
respect for others rights, values of scholarship and teaching. Students are expected to adhere to the institute rules
andregulations. AnyviolationwillbehandledaccordingtotherulessetforthbytheSenateandBoardofGovernors
ofIIITKottayam. Theadministratorsoftheinstitutewillnotifyparents/guardiansifastudentviolatestheCodeof
Conduct. Any of the following shall constitute violation of the Code of Conduct for students and makes the student
liable to disciplinary action by the Institute.
• Lack of courtesy and disorderly conduct or disruptive acts (within or outside Institute premises).
• Any act that compromises the safety/security of individuals or Institutional facilities.
• Willful damage or unauthorized removal of Institute property.
• Unauthorized access to institutional facilities/records.
• Tampering of data/records (reading, copying or destroying).
• Any act of fraud/misrepresentation/dishonesty.
• Misappropriation of any belongings of fellow students/staff/faculty.
• Adoption of unfair means during examinations or misconduct in research.
• Infringement of personal privacy.
• Ragging in any form.
• Caste/religion/ethnicity/gender/physical disability based discriminatory behaviour/remarks.
• Sexual harassment/assault.
• Possession of banned substances or dangerous items (illegal drugs, weapons, firearms etc.) that endangers
safety of student himself/herself or others.
• Any act that affects the reputation/orderly conduct of the institute.
R.13.2 The Disciplinary Procedure
1. The Discipline and Welfare Committee (DWC) of the Institute is constituted under the chairmanship of a
faculty member by the Director. Depending on the issues of allegations involved, the Chairman of the DWC
mayinviteadditionalmembers,forexampletheCoordinatorofaProgramme,studentsfacultyadviser/research
supervisor,DeputyRegistrar(Academics&Administration)incaseofacademicrelatedissues,tofacilitatewith
the investigation.
2. DWC will investigate the allegations of misdemeanours or violation of the Code of Conduct, without bias.
The DWC will subsequently submit a fact-finding report and recommend disciplinary action(s), if any, to the
Dean,StudentAffairs. Complaintsrelatedtocaste/religion/ethnicity/gender-specificdiscriminationandsexual
harassment will be investigated by an appropriate committee of the Institute and will report directly to the
Director.

even cancellation of an awarded Degree at any time.

• Fabrication includes making up data and recording them.

takenoutofthelibrary(includingpersonalitems,ifany)aretobeproducedforverificationbythecheckpoint
staff engaged in front of the library.
5. Studentsmustcarrytheiridentitycardsinsidethelibraryanditmustbeproducedwheneveraskedfor. Identity
card is mandatory for borrowing books from the Library.
6. Strict silence has to be maintained by all users in the library.
7. Use of mobile phones, consumption of food and drinks are strictly prohibited inside the library.
8. Use of the user PC kept inside the library is allowed only for accessing library catalogue, e- journals, e-books
and academic databases.
9. Return of book is mandatory before the due date. A fine of Rs. 1/- per day per book for the first week.
Renewal of a book is possible only if there is no pending reservation against it. A book may be recalled any
time before the due date, if it is urgently required by another member. A late fee of Rs. 10/- per day per book
will be imposed for the noncompliance with the requirement.
10. Any book, including reference books can be borrowed for overnight reference, at the closing time of the library
and to be returned at 9 AM on the next working day. Only one book can be borrowed for overnight reference.
A late fee of Rs. 50/- per day per book for the delayed return of such book will be charged.
11. Mutilation of books in any form (e.g. underlining, writing on pages, tearing off pages, damaging the binding
etc.) will lead to a heavy fine or even replacement of the book. Before borrowing a book users should ensure
the condition of the book and bring to the notice of the library staff, if any mutilation is found.
12. Members who lose/mutilate library books are liable to replace it with its latest edition along with a penalty of
20%ofthetotalcostofthebook. Allsuchreplacedbooksmustbeofthelatestedition. Ifthebookispartofa
set or series they may be called upon to replace the whole set or series. In case of the lost books is untraceable
in market or out of print Library Committee reserves the right to decide appropriate penalty.
13. Students must return all the books they borrowed before they go for vacation.
14. Users should obey the Library Rules and Regulations. Violation of rules and any act of misbehavior will be
brought to the notice of the Library Committee Chair, and will lead to strong disciplinary action.
R.14.2 Hostel Regulations
1. Students should be either in the hostel or in the Institute. Prior permission from the concerned warden and
matron have to be obtained in case the student plans to go anywhere else for a few hours. This has to be
recorded in the register kept with the matron/security in the Hostel.

happen without prior permission of the warden.
3. Leaving the hostel for a day or longer need prior permission from the faculty adviser of the student and the
Head of the Department with mandatory intimation to concerned matron and warden. Students are required
to fill up the leave application form available from the Academic Leave applications should be submitted at

least two working days in advance to the academic office. A copy of the approved leave form to be submitted
to the hostel caretaker/Security duly entering in the hostel register.

and is liable to pay for the damage.

the vacation, special permission has to be obtained from the competent authority in advance.
8. Anykindofloudnoiseintherooms,corridorsandpremisesofthehostel,especiallyduringnight,isprohibited.
9. Students are required to take care of their personal belongings, keep the respective rooms clean and the hostel
premises tidy.
10. Students are required to take utmost care for the hostel furniture, TV, washing machines, building structure,
electrical fittings etc.
11. In case of damage to any part of the hostel buildings, furniture, apparatus or other property of the institute,
caused by inmates of the hostel, the loss shall be recovered from the persons identified as responsible for such
damage. However, if the persons causing damage cannot be identified, the cost of repairing the same may be
assessedandwillbeleviedequallyamongstalltheinmatesofthehostelorgroupofinmatesofthehostelfound
responsible for the damage.
12. Students shall not paste any poster/picture on the walls or Vandalize etc., doors, windows and shelves. A fine
amount proportional to the damage caused shall be levied by the Warden/Competent authority.
13. Use of drugs/alcoholic beverages/tobacco products in the hostels is strictly prohibited. Smoking in public
is a punishable offence. Bringing substances which are prohibited by the laws of both State and Central
Governments(explosives,drugs,narcoticsandotherintoxicatingsubstances)totheHostel/InstitutePremises
is strictly prohibited and the guidelines and decision of the Antinarcotics cell / club of the Institute / local
administration will be binding on the students. Student shall not enter the hostel premises in intoxicated
state and should not possess such materials. Severe action (such as expulsion from hostel, rustication from the
Institute etc.) will be taken if any resident isfound violating this.
14. Studentsshouldstrictlyavoidgettingintoargumentswithfellowinmates,localitiesandsecurityofficers/matrons
of the hostel.

UGC REGULATIONS ON CURBING THE MENACE OF RAGGING IN
HIGHER EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS, 2009.

(under Section 26 (1)(g) of the University Grants Commission Act, 1956)
New Delhi-110002, the 17th June 2009

F.1-16/ 2007(CPP-IT)

PREAMBLE.

In view of the directions of the Hon’ble Supreme Court in the matter of
“University of Kerala v/s. Council, Principals, Colleges and others” in SLP no, 24295 of
2006 dated 16.05.2007 and that dated 8,05.2009 in Civil Appeal number 887 of 2009,
and in consideration of the determination of the Central Government and the University
Grants Commission to prohibit, prevent and eliminate the scourge of ragging including
any conduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or written or by an
act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a fresher or any
other student, or induiging in rowdy or indisciplined activities by any student or students
which causes or is likely to cause annoyance, hardship or psychological harm or to raise
fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any other student-or asking any student
te do any act which such student will not in the ordinary course do and which has the
effect of causing or generating a sense of shame, or torment or embarrassment so as
to adversely affect the physique or psyche of such fresher or any other student, with or
without an intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or showing off power, authority or
superiority by a student over any fresher or any other student, in all higher education
institutions in the country, and thereby, to provide for the healthy development,
physically and psychologically, of all students, the University Grants Commission, in
consultation with the Councils, brings forth this Regulation.

In exercise of the powers conferred by Clause-(g) of sub-section (1) of Section 26 of
the University Grants Commission Act, 1956, the University Grants Commission hereby

makes the following Regulations, namely;

§—139 GL/2009

1. Title, commencement and applicability. -

1.1 These regulations shall be called the “UGC Regulations on Curbing the Menace of
Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009”,

1.2 They shall come into force from the date of their publication in the Official
Gazette.

1.3 They shall apply to all the institutions coming within the definition of an
University under sub-section (f) of section (2) of the University Grants Commission Act,
1956, and to all institutions deemed to be a university under Section 3 of the University
Grants Commission Act, 1956, to all other higher educational institutions, or elements of
such universities or institutions, including its departments, constituent units and all the
premises, whether being academic, residential, playgrounds, canteen, or other such
Premises of such universities, deemed universities and higher educational! institutions,
whether located within the campus or outside, and to all means of transportation of
students, whether public or private, accessed by students for the pursuit of studies in
such universities, deemed universities and higher educational institutions.

2. Objectives,-

To prohibit any conduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or
written or by an act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a
fresher or any other student, or indulging in rowdy or indisciplined activities by any
student or students which causes or is lkely to cause. annoyance, hardship or
psychological harm or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any other
student or asking any student to do any act which such student will not in the ordinary
course do and which has the effect of causing or generating a sense of shame, or
torment or embarrassment SO as to adversely affect the physique or psyche of such
fresher or any other Student, with or without an intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or
showing off power, authority or superiority by @ student over any fresher or any other
student; and thereby, to eliminate ragging in ail its forms from universities, deemed
universities and other higher educational institutions in the country by prohibiting it
