under these Regulations, preventing its occurrence and punishing those who indulge in

raggin 9 as provicied for in these Regulations and the appropriate law in force.

3. What constitutes Ragging.- Ragging constitutes one or more of any of the
following acts:

a.

any coriduct by any student or students whether by words spoken or written or
by an ‘act which has the effect of teasing, treating or handling with rudeness a
fresher or any other student;

indulging in rowdy or indisciplined activities by any student or students which
causes or is likely to cause: annoyance, hardship, physical or psychological harm
or to raise fear or apprehension thereof in any fresher or any other student;
asking any student to do any act which such student wii not in the ordinary
course do and which has, the effect of causing or generating a sense of sharne,
or torment or embarrassment so as to adversely affect the physique or psyche
of such fresher or any other student;

any act by a senior student that prevents, disrupts or disturbs the regular
academic activity of any other student or a fresher;

exploiting the services of a fresher or any other student for completing the
academic tasks assigned to an individual or a group of students.

any act of financial extortion or forceful expenditure burden put on a fresher or
any other student by students;

any act: of physical abuse including all variants of it: sexual abuse, homosexual
assaults, stripping, forcing obscene and lewd acts, gestures, causing bodily harm
or any other danger to health or person;

any act or abuse by spoken words, emails, past, public insults which would also
include deriving perverted pleasure, vicarious or sadistic thrill from actively or
passively participating in the discomfiture to fresher or any other student ;

any act that affects the mental health and self-confidence of a fresher or any
other student

with or without an intent to derive a sadistic pleasure or showing off power, authority or

superiority by a student over any fresher or any other student.

4. Definitions.-

4)

In these regulations unless the context otherwise requires,-

a) “Act” means, the University Grants Commission Act, 1956 (3 of 1956);

b) “acacernic year” means the period from the commencement of admission of
students in any course of study in the institution up to the completion of
academic requirements for that particular year.

¢) “Anti-Ragging Helpline” means the Helpline established under clause (a) of
Regulation 8.1 of these Regulations.

d) “Coramission” means the University Grants Commission;

e) “Council” means a body so constituted by an Act of Parliament or an Act of
any Sitate Legislature for setting, Or co-ordinating or maintaining standards in the
relevant areas of higher education, such as the All India Council for Technical
Education (AICTE), the Bar Council of India (BCI), the Dental Council of India
(DCT), the Distance Education Council (DEC), the Indian Council of Agricultural
Research ({CAR), the Indian Nursing Council (INC), the Medical Council of India
(MCI), the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE), the Pharmacy Counc
of India (PCI), etc. and the State Higher Education Councils.

f) “District Level Anti- Ragging Committee” means the Committee, headed by
the: District Magistrate, constituted by the State Government, for the control and
elircination of ragging in institutions within the jurisdiction of the district.

gq) “Head of the institution” means the Vice-Chancellor in case of a university or a
deemed to be university, the Principal or the Director or such other designation
as the executive head of the institution of the college is referred.

h) “Fresher” means 4 student who has been admitted to an institution and who
is undergoing his/her first year of study in such institution.

to an university, # deemed to be university, 4 college, an institute, an institution

to, but not necessarily culminating in, a degree (graduate, postgraduate and/or

Respected Madam/Sir,

In pursuance to the Judgement of the Hon’ble Supreme Court of India dated 08.05.2009 in Civil Appeal
No. 887/2009, the UGC had notified “Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational
Institutions, 2009”. The Regulations are available on the UGC website i.e. www.ugc.ac.in. These regulations are
mandatory for all higher educational institutions across the country.

As multiple mechanisms are required to ensure a ragging-free campus, here are some recommendations
and action steps which are need to be taken by your esteemed university and all institutions under your ambit.

A. Basic Measures:

1. Constitution of anti-ragging committee, anti-ragging squad, setting up of Anti-Ragging Cell and adequate
publicity for these measures through various media.

2. A clear mention of anti-ragging warning in the institution’s prospectus and information booklets /brochures
shall be ensured.

3. Preparation of e-admission booklet or brochure, e-leaflets of your institutions giving detailed guidance to
admitted students in case of ragging, instead of print/hard copy.

4. Display of banners/posters at conspicuous places in the campus to create awareness on anti-ragging
measures amongst students (soft copy of the posters attached are also available on UGC website
www.uge.ac.in & www.antiragging.in)

5. Updation of websites of institutions with the complete address and contact details of nodal officers related to
anti-ragging committee.

6. An online undertaking in every academic year ‘to be submitted by each student and every parent, in
compliance with the UGC Regulations and its 2"' Amendment regarding submission of undertaking.

7. UGC has notified 3 Amendment in UGC Regulations on 29" June, 2016 to expand the definition of ragging
by including the following:

“3. (i) Any act of physical or mental abuse (including bullying and exclusion) targeted at another student
(fresher or otherwise) on the ground of colour, race, religion, caste, ethnicity, gender (including
transgender), sexual orientation, appearance, nationality, regional origins, linguistic identity, place of birth,
place of residence or economic background.”

8. Installation of CCTV cameras at vital points.

B. Counseling and monitoring measures

1. Regular interaction and counseling with the students to detect early signs of ragging and identification of
trouble-triggers.

2. Surprise inspection at hostels, students’ accommodation, canteens, rest-cum-recreation rooms, toilets,
bus-stands and any other measure which would augur well in preventing/quelling ragging and any uncalled

for behaviour/incident. .

C. Creative Dissemination of the idea of ragging-free campus
1. Events like Anti-Ragging workshops, seminars and other creative avenues to spread the idea.
2. Safety and security apps without affecting the privacy of individuals can be creatively deployed.
D. Using other UGC initiated measures

1. Students in distress due to ragging related incidents can call the National Anti-Ragging Helpline 1800-180-5522
(24x7 Toll Free) or e-mail the Anti-Ragging Helpline at helpline@antiragging.in.

INDIAN INSTITUTE OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
KOTTAYAM
HALLS OF RESIDENCE
RULES AND REGULATIONS
1. Movement and Presence on Campus
1.1 Students are expected to remain within the Institute premises or in the hostel throughout
the duration of the semester.
1.2 Leaving the Institute campus during academic hours is strictly prohibited, unless prior
permission has been granted by the concerned authority.
2. Night Return and Departure Timings
2.1 All students are strictly prohibited from roaming the campus after 9:30 PM. After this
time, students must either return to their respective hostels or remain inside their designated
classrooms for study purposes only, up until 10:30 PM.
2.2 All students must return to their respective hostels by 11:00 PM. Students cannot leave
the hostels after 11:00 PM. Parents of defaulters shall be contacted, and in case such
activities occur without prior permission of the Warden and missing report may be filed
with the local police.
3. Leave and Absence from Campus
3.1 Students must obtain permission through the Flee Outpass portal
(https://outpass.iiitkottayam.ac.in/) or the Biometric Outpass system
(https://gatepassstud.iiitkottayam.ac.in/) before leaving campus during weekends or non-
academic hours, provided the duration of absence does not exceed one day.
3.2 Students leaving the campus using the RFID/Biometric Outpass System should return
to the campus before 9:30 PM. Upon re-entry, in-campus students must register their return
at the Institute's Main Gate, while off-campus students shall register their return at their
respective hostels.
3.3 For any absence involving an overnight stay outside the campus, students are required
to submit a leave form (available from the Academic Office/Hostel Office), approved by
their Faculty Advisor and the concerned hostel Warden/Assistant Wardens.
3.4 Students going for an internship must submit the leave form for the period duly approved
by their Faculty Advisor, the Warden/Assistant Wardens and the corresponding HoD.
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam

4. Permanent Address and Contact Details
Permanent address, including phone numbers of parent(s)/guardian(s), must be given to the
Warden/IIIT Office. Change in address/contact numbers shall be updated whenever occurs.
5. Interchange of Rooms/Hostels
5.1 Students are not permitted to interchange or swap rooms/hostels without obtaining prior
approval from the Warden/Chief Warden/Associate Dean (Hostel Affairs). Any request for
room swapping shall be submitted using the prescribed Room Swap Application Form,
available with the Hostel Manager or at the Security Desk.
5.2 Residents shall occupy only the room officially allotted to them. No resident shall permit
any student who is not officially allotted to the room, or any student whose hostel
accommodation has been suspended (as a disciplinary action) or cancelled, to stay in or
occupy the room.
5.3 Any violation of the above shall be treated as a serious act of misconduct and shall attract
severe disciplinary action, including the imposition of a fine, expulsion from the hostel, and
any other action deemed appropriate by the Institute.
6. Responsibility for Damage to Property
The resident(s) of the room are responsible for any damage to the property in the room
during their occupancy and are liable to pay for the damage. Furthermore, any act of
indiscipline or misconduct occurring within the room, including those involving visitors or
other students, shall be considered the responsibility of the resident(s) as well.
7. Vacation Stay
All students must vacate the hostel during vacation time. If any student wishes to stay back
during the vacation, special permission must be obtained from the competent authority in
advance. An additional mess fee and hostel fee will be levied based on the duration of the
extended stay.
8. Noise Prohibition
Any kind of loud noise in the rooms, corridors, or premises of the hostel, especially during
the night (after 11 PM), is prohibited.
9. Cleanliness and Personal Belongings
Students are required to take care of their personal belongings, keep their respective rooms
clean, and maintain tidy hostel premises. Waste shall not be littered and plastic bottles must
be disposed of only in the designated waste bins.
10. Care of Hostel Property
Students are required to take utmost care of the hostel furniture, TV, washing machines,
building structure, electrical fittings, etc.
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam

11. Unidentified Damage
In case of damage to any part of the hostel buildings, furniture, apparatus, or other property
of the Institute caused by inmates of the hostel, the loss shall be recovered from the persons
identified as responsible. However, if the persons causing damage cannot be identified, the
cost of repairing the same may be assessed and levied equally amongst all inmates of the
hostel or the group found responsible.
12. Defacement and Vandalism
12.1 Students shall not paste posters or pictures, scribble on walls, or vandalize doors,
windows, shelves, or any other hostel property. A fine proportionate to the damage caused
will be levied by the Warden or other competent authority.
12.2 If any such damage or defacement is found during the first entry into the allotted room,
the student must immediately report it in writing to the respective Assistant Warden or
Warden.
12.3 Failure to do so may result in the student being held responsible for the damage.
13. Prohibition of Intoxicants and Banned Substances
13.1 The use, possession, or consumption of drugs, alcoholic beverages, tobacco products,
or any intoxicating substances, fireworks, hazardous chemicals is strictly prohibited within
the hostel or institute premises. Smoking is also not permitted under any circumstances.
13.2 Bringing or storing items that are banned under State or Central Government laws —
including but not limited to explosives, narcotics, and other controlled substances — into
the Hostel or Institute premises is a serious offense.
13.3 The guidelines and directives issued by the Institute's Anti-Narcotics Cell/Club and/or
the local administration shall be binding on all students.
13.4 Violation of these regulations will attract severe disciplinary action, which may include
expulsion from the hostel, rustication from the Institute, or other penalties as deemed
appropriate by the authorities including registering of complaint with the law enforcement
agencies.
14. Conduct with Others
Residents shall treat wardens, hostel staff, locals, security personnel, housekeeping staff,
mess workers, and fellow residents with dignity and respect.
15. Cooking and Electrical Appliances
Cooking inside the rooms is strictly prohibited. Students are not permitted to use heaters,
electric irons, or similar appliances of any kind consuming electricity in the rooms. Close
water taps after use.
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam

16. Guests
Guests are strictly prohibited from entering hostels rooms. Visiting hours are permitted only
until 7:00 PM, and all guest meetings shall be restricted to the designated area at the main
entrance, adjacent to the security guard's post. No guest shall be permitted beyond this point
under any circumstances.
17. Emergency Contact
In case of any emergency (illness, accidents, etc.), contact the concerned Warden/Assistant
Wardens/Security Officer/Hostel Manager.
18. Electrical Safety and Fines
All electrical appliances and equipment must be switched off after use or whenever all
occupants leave the room to ensure safety and conserve energy. If found otherwise, a fine
will be levied, including recovery of the cost of electrical equipment/fittings/appliances, etc.
19. Loss of Personal Belongings
Residents are advised to take proper care of their personal belongings and ensure that their
rooms are securely locked whenever left unoccupied. Institute/hostel authorities/wardens
are not responsible for any loss, damage, or theft of any such items kept by inmates.
20. Furniture Movement
The resident shall not move any furniture/appliance from its proper allotted room/place.
21. Outdoor Games and Celebrations
21.1 Students are strictly prohibited from playing outdoor games such as cricket, football,
volleyball, badminton, etc., in the corridors, balconies, wings, or any other common areas
within the hostel premises, as these activities may cause damage to property or disturb
fellow residents.
21.2 Birthday celebrations are permitted only in the designated open area adjacent to the
hostel and must be conducted in the presence of the hostel security in-charge. If Institute
property such as chairs or tables is used for the celebration, it must be returned promptly in
good condition after the event.
21.3 All such celebrations must conclude by 12.00 -12:30 AM, beyond which no further
activity will be permitted.
21.4 Beating or any type of physical assault as part of birthday celebrations is strictly
prohibited.
22. Maintenance Works
Students should cooperate while maintenance works are carried out and vacate their rooms
completely when the maintenance section requires the rooms for this purpose. On such
occasions, students shall be provided alternate accommodation.
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam

23. Vacating Procedure
23.1 Students going on vacation or leave are required to remove their belongings from the
room and place them in the common storeroom assigned for this purpose with proper
marking. They must hand over the room key to the security personnel or caretaker staff after
making the necessary entry in the register.
23.2 Students must also clear all dues and obtain a No-Dues Certificate in order to vacate
the hostel during vacation.
24. Loss of Keys/Lock
Cost of replacement of the lock and keys shall be paid/recovered.
25. Safety and Security
For safety and security, students are strictly advised not to climb rocks/mountains or go into
forest areas, bushes, or nearby private properties.
26. Anti-Ragging Regulations
The Institute's anti-ragging regulations must be strictly followed in the hostels as well.
27. In/Out Register
Students must record their entry and exit in the In/Out Register maintained at the caretaker's
desk of their respective hostel. Any instance of forgery or signing on behalf of others will
be treated as a strict violation and attract disciplinary action. All students must sign/complete
biometric attendance between 9:30 PM to 11:00 PM in the hostel In/Out register.
28. Knowledge of Rules
Every student must familiarize themselves with all hostel rules and regulations and adhere
to them strictly. Ignorance of the rules will not be accepted as an excuse.
29. Grievance Redressal
It is the responsibility of hostel inmates to keep their rooms tidy. Any sort of grievance or
complaint shall be recorded in the complaint register available at the desk of the security in-
charge. If appropriate remedial action is not taken within three working days, the student
may escalate the complaint to their corresponding Assistant Warden or Warden.
30. Hostel Timings
 Outpass/Gate In: 9:00 PM
 Move to hostel from academic/hostel premises: 9:30 PM
 Move to hostel from classrooms: 10:30 PM
 Hostel main door closes: 11:00 PM
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam

31. Vehicle Timing for Off-Campus Students
Off-campus students must travel to and from the Institute strictly according to the trip
schedule. Any violation may lead to overcrowding in subsequent trips and will not be
permitted.
32. Online Food Deliveries
All online food deliveries must be recorded in the register at the hostel security desk.
33. Indoor Games
Indoor games are strictly prohibited after 9:30 PM.
34. Visiting Other Hostels
Students are strictly prohibited from visiting other hostels.
35. Silence Hours
Silence hours will be observed from 11 PM to 6.00 AM on all days. No noise of any sort
will be permitted. Residents shall not go to others' rooms and disturb the inmates.
Complaints from other residents will be investigated, and action will be taken accordingly.
36. Pets and Stray Animals
Pets of all kinds are prohibited inside the hostel. Feeding stray dogs or cats in the
hostel/institute premises is not permitted.
37. Room Inspection
The Institute reserves the right to inspect any hostel room whenever necessary in the interest
of safety, security, maintenance, hygiene, or investigation of disciplinary matters.
38. CCTV and Digital Misconduct
38.1 CCTV surveillance may be used in common areas of the hostel for safety and security
purposes.
38.2 Recording, photographing, or publishing images/videos of hostel residents without
consent from competent authorities is prohibited.
39. Amendment
These rules may be modified, amended, or supplemented by the Institute from time to time.
Such amendments shall become effective from the date of notification.
VIOLATION OF ANY OF THE ABOVE RULES SHALL MAKE THE STUDENT
LIABLE TO DISCIPLINARY ACTION BY THE INSTITUTE.
Hostel Rules and Regulations – July 2026
Indian Institute of Information Technology Kottayam
